statement: A digit string is good when every digit at an even index (0, 2, 4, …) is even (0, 2, 4, 6 or 8) and every digit at an odd index is a prime (2, 3, 5 or 7). Digit strings may start with 0.
Given an integer n, return how many good digit strings of length n there are. The number can be very large, so return it modulo 10⁹ + 7.

A string of length n has ⌈n / 2⌉ even indices with 5 choices each and ⌊n / 2⌋ odd indices with 4 choices each, so the answer is 5^⌈n/2⌉ × 4^⌊n/2⌋ mod 10⁹ + 7, computed with fast modular exponentiation.

examples.explanation: Indices 0 and 2 have 5 choices each and indices 1 and 3 have 4 choices each, so there are 5² × 4² = 400 good strings.
Index 0 has 5 choices and index 1 has 4, giving 5 × 4 = 20 good strings, such as "02" and "87".
